title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: Directors, employees, consultants and contractors of Metals X and its related entities. Bound by the general insider trading ban, prohibited periods, and the excluded-trading and hardship exceptions; not subject to the standing preclearance, hedging, margin loan or non-discretionary trading plan rules that apply only to Senior Management.

tiers.name: Senior Management
tiers.description: The Board, the Chief Executive Officer or any other senior executives, and the Company Secretary. Must obtain prior written approval from the Chairman (or two directors in his absence) before any trading, and separately before hedging their holding, entering margin loan/secured lending arrangements, or putting in place a non-discretionary trading plan.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board; a subset of Senior Management distinguished by an additional obligation to notify the Company Secretary of securities held on appointment and of any change within 2 days.

tiers.name: Family member
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, parents or parents-in-law, children/stepchildren, and the spouses/partners of those people. Dealing by a family member during a prohibited period is only 'discouraged', not prohibited.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may notify Staff of any other prohibited period when it is considering matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A; no confidentiality provision is stated. Trading is also barred, independent of any window, at any time Metals X is in possession of unpublished price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Securities are defined to include 'any financial products issued or created over or in respect of Metals X securities' with no venue limit, so an OTC put/call is a dealing; Senior Management must obtain the Chairman's (or two directors') prior written approval before any trading, not only during a prohibited period.
rules.evidence: Senior Management is required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

rules.detail: For Staff who are not Senior Management, no standing preclearance is required for a derivative dealing; it is only subject to the general prohibited-period and inside-information rules.
rules.evidence: securities are any listed or unlisted class of share, right, option, warrant, convertible note, bond, debenture, or any financial products issued or created over or in respect of Metals X securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban at any time, not limited to prohibited periods, on hedging unvested entitlements under equity-based remuneration schemes.
rules.evidence: Senior management are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of a vested security holding requires prior written approval under the section 10 procedure (Chairman, or two directors in his absence).
rules.evidence: Senior management must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written approval in accordance with the procedure set out in section 10.

rules.detail: For Staff generally (not limited to Senior Management), hedging financial products over unvested entitlements is banned only during a prohibited period; the policy does not separately address it outside a prohibited period for non-Senior-Management staff.
rules.evidence: The dealing in financial products issued or granted over or in respect of Metals X securities which have the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements is prohibited during a prohibited period.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a structure that limits economic risk of unvested entitlements is caught by the absolute hedging ban.
rules.evidence: Senior management are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

Staff, who are not in the possession of price sensitive information, may be given prior written clearance by the Board to sell or otherwise dispose of Metals X during a prohibited period, where the Staff is in severe financial difficulties or other exceptional circumstances determined by the Board.
such as required under a court order, in a bona fide family settlement, or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

exemption_authority: The Board may, in its discretion, give prior written clearance to Staff who are not in possession of price sensitive information to sell or dispose of securities during a prohibited period in cases of severe financial difficulties or other exceptional circumstances (court order, bona fide family settlement, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement). Senior Management may also, under section 7, cancel a non-discretionary trading plan during a prohibited period only in exceptional circumstances with prior written approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Senior Management is required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman ... prior to any trading being undertaken.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require clearance inside a closed period, MLX requires the Chairman's (or two directors') written approval before every trade by Senior Management, so entry, roll, and unwind of a collar and its loan each need fresh clearance regardless of the calendar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Senior management must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan in respect of Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval ... Senior management must not cancel any such trading plan during a Prohibited Period, unless the circumstances are exceptional and the procedure for prior written approval ... has been met.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a collar's settlement or unwind mechanics are structured as a non-discretionary trading plan, separate approval is required, and it cannot be cancelled inside a closed period without exceptional-circumstances approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing in Metals X securities during a prohibited period by a family member is to be discouraged.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is soft, non-binding language rather than a prohibition, so routing a collar or loan through a family member during a closed period is not itself a breach of this policy, though general insider trading law and reputational risk still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (the policy distinguishes only 'unvested entitlements' from a general 'security holding'; it never refers to a holding lock)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once shares vest, they appear to be treated as an ordinary security holding available for hedging or security with clearance, with no intermediate holding-locked state to navigate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy only provides a summary of applicable legal and regulatory issues which are complex, and should therefore only be used as a general guide, not as legal advice.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy disclaims completeness, so a collar structure cleared under this policy still needs independent Corporations Act and market-manipulation analysis.

summary: A funded collar over vested Metals X shares held by Senior Management (the Board, CEO/senior executives and the Company Secretary) is achievable, but sections 3.3/10.1 require prior written approval from the Chairman (or two directors in his absence) before any trade at any time, and both the hedging clause (section 5) and the margin loan/secured lending clause (section 6) separately require that same approval for the put/call legs and for the loan secured on the shares. Hedging of unvested entitlements under an equity incentive scheme is banned outright for Senior Management with no clearance route, so the collar and loan can only be written over vested holdings. Ordinary Staff face no comparable clearance requirement for either the derivatives or the financing leg, only the prohibited-period and inside-information restrictions, and family-member trading during a prohibited period is merely 'discouraged' rather than banned. Execution must avoid the annual, half-year and quarterly closed periods and any inside information, directors must report resulting holding changes to the Company Secretary within 2 days, and any plan-style unwind mechanism needs its own separate approval.
